visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A man with glasses and a black shirt stands in front of a dark shelf filled with bottles, speaking energetically with hand gestures. (2) A variety of cultural images appear, including a wooden panel featuring the colorful Eight Auspicious Signs, a 2025 Thangka calendar with a central deity, and a close-up of hands joined in prayer. (3) The man returns to the screen, followed by images of a Buddhist altar with small golden bowls and a tapestry showing two golden fish. (4) Footage shows elderly people practicing Tai Chi in a park, then transitions back to the man and then to images of prayer wheels and a blooming pink lotus. (5) An image of a historical figure, Zhou Dunyi, is shown followed by a Thangka painting and detailed shots of Mongolian horse saddles and yurts (Gers). (6) The man continues speaking, interspersed with shots of a white airplane landing and the red-and-white exterior of the Museum of Mongol and Tibetan Culture. (7) The final sequence showcases various artifacts inside the museum, including ceramics, metalwork, and a master's memorial hall with religious objects in glass displays, ending with the man inviting viewers to the exhibition.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio features a high-energy male voice speaking at a rapid, excited pace, explaining the origins of cultural symbols. The background is filled with a bright, high-tempo electronic pop track with a steady, driving drum beat. (2) Sharp 'whoosh' sound effects punctuate every visual cut, which occurs roughly every 1.5 seconds. (3) Subtle digital UI clicks and 'pop' SFX are used to synchronize with the appearance of text overlays and variety graphics. (4) The host's tone remains consistent—authoritative yet friendly—throughout the track, with no background ambient noise interfering with the studio-clean vocal signal. (5) The music continues as a constant rhythmic bed until the final second, where a sharp hard cut ends both the vocal and musical layers simultaneously.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This video serves as a high-energy educational and promotional piece for an exhibition at the Museum of Mongol and Tibetan Culture in Taipei. It aims to connect familiar auspicious symbols in daily life to their deep roots in Mongolian and Tibetan traditions, thereby sparking interest in the museum's current showcase.
